properties.title: medDreamer: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning with Latent Imagination on Complex EHRs for Clinical Decision Support

membership.reason: Dreamer-style RSSM patient world model with Adaptive Feature Integration for irregular/missing EHRs coupled to two-phase actor-critic policy optimization.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L4 decision-coupled MBRL world model (WT_EHR, BP_CONTROLLER).

properties.backbone: AFI irregular-data encoder + RSSM (256D GRU + 32D stochastic latent) + reward/continue/actor-critic MLPs

properties.flow: Irregular EHR (o_t, Delta_t, m_t) -> AFI + RSSM world model -> Phase 1 hybrid (tau=10) + Phase 2 imagined (H=15) actor-critic -> sepsis/MV treatment policy

properties.purpose: Offline RL treatment recommendation for ICU sepsis (IV fluids, vasopressors) and mechanical ventilation (PEEP, FiO2, tidal volume).

assertions.rationale: Explicit missingness masks m_t in {0,1}^d processed by AFI module.
Adaptive Feature Integration (AFI) consumes elapsed intervals Delta_t without coarse time discretization.
AFI encoder mapping irregular, sparse clinical observations into RSSM latent state.
Observation reconstruction head o_hat_t used to train the world model.
256D GRU deterministic + 32D stochastic RSSM latent patient state.
Discrete clinical treatment actions (IV fluid/vasopressor bins; PEEP/FiO2/tidal volume).
Learned RSSM latent dynamics world model.
Next latent state conditioned on clinician or policy action a_t.
Actor-critic policy trained in two phases via hybrid real+imagined and full imagined world-model rollouts.

Two-phase actor-critic policy learning over hybrid real+imagined (tau=10) and full imagined (H=15) RSSM trajectories is evaluated on MIMIC-IV sepsis (21,233 patients) and eICU mechanical ventilation (21,595 patients) against model-free and model-based baselines (Table 1, p. 8) and ablated across MDP1 Only, MDP2 Only, E2E, ActorCritic, Curriculum, and imagination horizons tau/H (Table 2, p. 12). Outcome is mixed because evaluation is retrospective OPE only (sepsis WIS 9.25 < CQL 10.42/BCQ 10.13, and sepsis estimated mortality 14.25% falls outside its reported 95% CI [14.6, 17.5] in Table 1 / [14.6, 15.7] in p. 9 text).
Personalized ICU sepsis and mechanical ventilation treatment decision support.
Policy action distributions stratified by SOFA severity and mortality vs clinician-divergence V-curves (Figs. 2-5).
Off-policy evaluation (WIS, WPDIS, CWPDIS) and estimated mortality (14.25% sepsis, 12.44% MV) across MIMIC-IV and eICU.
Evaluated across two distinct large-scale ICU databases (MIMIC-IV and eICU).
Imagined rollouts execute entirely in RSSM latent space.

evidence_fragments.content: To address these limitations, we propose medDreamer, a novel model-based reinforcement learning framework for personalized treatment recommendation. medDreamer contains a world model with an Adaptive Feature Integration module that simulates latent patient states from irregular data and a two-phase policy trained on a hybrid of real and imagined trajectories.

Figure 1: Our medDreamer architecture is divided into two stages: World model training and Policy training. The world model uses time interval ∆t, observation o t and clinician action a t to learn patient latent dynamics through reconstruction and predict reward ˆr t. Policy training consists of two phases: In Phase 1 we use T steps of states generated from real clinical decisions and imagine τ steps into the future and train the policy using the concatenated states. In Phase 2 we use full imagined trajectories of length H.

For sepsis treatment, we use the large-scale MIMIC-IV [ 17] database, extracting 21,233 adult septic patients. We exclude patients with missing mortality outcomes or demographics, those with treatment withdrawal or multiple ICU stays. Each trajectory starts 24 hours before diagnosis and ends at 48 hours post-diagnosis. Each observation has 40 physiological features, and the outcome is 90-day mortality. For MV management, we use the eICU Collaborative Research (eICU)[38] database, and extract patients aged ≥16 who received MV for at least 24 hours. We also exclude patients with missing mortality outcomes or demographics, those ventilated for >14 days, and those with missing interventions. After filtering, 21,595 patients were retained with 41 physiological features, and the outcome is hospital mortality.

Figure 2: Differences between clinicians’ actions and policy actions for sepsis task. Figure 3: Differences between clinicians’ actions and policy actions for MV task. Figure. 5 shows the difference in recommended dosages between the policy and clinicians, and corresponding mortality. Except for high SOFA, all groups show a distinct V-shaped pattern, where mortality is lowest when the policy aligns with clinician decisions (i.e., x=0) and increases in divergence when in either direction.

We imagine 10 steps for phase 1 and 15 steps for phase 2. All models use the same decoder, reward predictor, continue predictor, and actor critic based on MLP with 2 hidden layers of size 512 with layer norm and a SiLU activation. The dynamics model uses a GRU cell with a 256-dimensional hidden state and a stochastic latent space of size 32.

locator.section_or_table: Section 4.2.1 RQ1 OPE and Mortality Results

evidence_fragments.content: For the sepsis task, medDreamer obtains the highest scores in WPDIS and CWPDIS, as well as the lowest estimated mortality rate of 14.25%, with a narrow 95% confidence interval [14.6, 15.7], suggesting reliable estimation. While model-free baselines such as EZ-Vent and DeepVent achieve stronger WIS scores, WIS is known to be sensitive to large importance ratios and can exhibit high variance. Thus, a lower WIS score does not necessarily indicate inferior performance, especially when not considered alongside weighted or cumulatively weighted variants. In contrast, CWPDIS is typically more stable and indicative of generalization beyond the behavior policy, where medDreamer demonstrates superior values. For the MV task, medDreamer again outperforms all baselines in WIS, WPDIS, CWPDIS, and achieves the lowest estimated mortality rate of 12.44% [11.42, 13.45], outperforming model-free methods and Dreamer.

There is a clear improvement in all the metrics when moving from phase 1 to phase 2, simply training on partially imagined trajectories is not sufficient to fully explore the data. Directly training on full imagined data surprisingly shows good results, indicating that our world model is able to create meaningful trajectories that are beneficial for policy learning.

capability_assessments.rationale: medDreamer implements a persistent RSSM patient latent state (256D GRU + 32D stochastic: 019) with learned temporal latent dynamics and AFI irregular-EHR encoding (041, 042), coupled to two-phase actor-critic policy optimization over latent imagination rollouts (tau=10, H=15) evaluated via offline OPE (WIS/WPDIS/CWPDIS) and estimated mortality across MIMIC-IV sepsis and eICU MV cohorts plus two-phase/horizon ablations (063, 120; Tables 1-2). Supports offline/retrospective L4 only (R2); does not establish causal identification or prospective clinical treatment efficacy.

limitations: Offline retrospective evaluation relies on off-policy importance sampling (WIS/WPDIS/CWPDIS) rather than prospective clinical deployment.
No prospective clinician-in-the-loop or patient safety trial.
Table 1 (p. 8) reports medDreamer sepsis estimated mortality 14.25% with 95% CI [14.6, 17.5], while p. 9 text states [14.6, 15.7]—the point estimate falls outside both reported confidence intervals.

legacy_cells.B: medDreamer: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning with Latent Imagination on Complex EHRs for Clinical Decision Support
legacy_cells.O: Sepsis; acute respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation; renal replacement therapy (appendix task)
legacy_cells.S: Can a policy trained using irregular EHR-derived latent patient states and imagined futures recommend treatment actions associated with higher estimated return and lower estimated mortality?
legacy_cells.T: MIMIC-IV: 21,233 adult septic patients; eICU: 21,595 patients aged ≥16 who received mechanical ventilation for at least 24 hours.
legacy_cells.V: Treatment recommendations for sepsis (IV fluids and vasopressors) and mechanical ventilation management; appendix also evaluates renal replacement therapy.
legacy_cells.X: F2 EHR / ICU event & latent patient dynamics
legacy_cells.AI: EHR physiological measurements (vitals, laboratory values, demographics); observation masks and elapsed-time intervals; clinician treatment actions
legacy_cells.AJ: Adaptive Feature Integration (AFI): separate linear projections of observations and elapsed intervals, combined through a Factorization Machine; GRU posterior/prior dynamics.
legacy_cells.AN: AFI explicitly represents observed-value masks and elapsed intervals; reconstruction loss masks missing targets and does not propagate their gradients.
legacy_cells.AS: Stochastic latent space size 32; GRU hidden state 256 dimensions.
legacy_cells.AT: Posterior update qφ(s_t | s_{t−1}, a_{t−1}, encoded observation_t); prior transition predicts from preceding latent state and action.
legacy_cells.BD: Sepsis: IV-fluid and vasopressor doses each discretized into four quantile bins plus no treatment, forming 25 joint actions. Ventilation: PEEP, FiO₂, and IBW-adjusted tidal volume combined into 18 discrete actions (low/medium/high levels).
legacy_cells.BS: Latent-state reconstruction of clinical observations, predicted immediate reward, and predicted continuation/termination.
legacy_cells.BT: Reward, continuation, reconstruction, actor, and critic heads.
legacy_cells.BU: Task-specific reward: sepsis uses SOFA/lactate changes and terminal survival; ventilation uses SpO₂ and mean blood pressure ranges and terminal survival.
legacy_cells.BV: World-model objective combines reward symlog two-hot likelihood, continuation Bernoulli likelihood, masked symlog-squared reconstruction loss, and prior/posterior KL (ELBO); policy uses REINFORCE actor loss and a return-distribution critic loss.
legacy_cells.CK: Maximize discounted expected task reward; reward encodes SOFA/lactate improvement and terminal survival for sepsis, or SpO₂/mean blood pressure targets and terminal survival for ventilation.
legacy_cells.CX: No counterfactual ground-truth validation is reported; authors state the retrospective observational evaluation lacks counterfactual ground truth.
legacy_cells.DN: MIMIC-IV; eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU); AmsterdamUMCdb (appendix)
legacy_cells.EA: Qualitative reconstruction assessment: MBP trajectories reconstructed by medDreamer were described as temporally aligned with ground truth, including under increased missingness.
legacy_cells.EC: Offline policy evaluation: sepsis WPDIS 0.27 and CWPDIS 0.19; mechanical-ventilation WIS 24.06, WPDIS 0.32, CWPDIS 0.25. Authors report estimated MV mortality 12.44% (95% CI 11.42–13.45); this is not observed prospective benefit.
legacy_cells.EJ: Compared with Dreamer, MBRL-BNN, and MBRL-GMM; authors report medDreamer had higher WPDIS/CWPDIS on both main tasks. The paper also reports model-free baselines including DDQN, EZ-Vent, and DeepVent.
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations compare AFI vs nearest-neighbor-imputed encoder, Phase-1-only and Phase-2-only training, end-to-end training, actor-critic and curriculum variants, and varied imagined lengths τ and H.
legacy_cells.EL: Dreamer reportedly struggled to converge because of instability in joint end-to-end training; high-SOFA action/mortality patterns were less consistent.
legacy_cells.EM: Two-phase policy training grounds Phase 1 in real clinical trajectories with short imagined continuations, then refines on imagined trajectories; no prospective safety mechanism was evaluated.
legacy_cells.EO: Study datasets are described as anonymous and deidentified.
legacy_cells.ER: MIMIC-IV reviewed by the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Centre IRB (number 2001-P-001699/14), with waiver of informed consent; eICU approved by the MIT IRB.
legacy_cells.FL: AFI encodes EHR observations, masks, and elapsed time; a recurrent stochastic latent patient state is updated by a GRU posterior and predicted by a GRU prior conditioned on actions; reward, continuation, and observation-reconstruction heads support an actor–critic policy trained in two imagination phases.
legacy_cells.FM: Authors contribute an AFI world model for irregular EHR data, a two-phase hybrid real/imagined policy-training framework, and evaluation on sepsis and mechanical-ventilation tasks.
legacy_cells.FN: For main tasks, authors report sepsis WPDIS 0.27/CWPDIS 0.19 and MV WIS 24.06/WPDIS 0.32/CWPDIS 0.25; estimated MV mortality is reported as 12.44% (95% CI 11.42–13.45). These are offline estimates, not measured patient outcomes.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors state that experiments use retrospective observational data and lack counterfactual ground truth; reward-based estimates may not capture true clinical utility; generalizability beyond tested tasks, hospitals, or populations remains unestablished; clinician-trust assessment is needed before deployment.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors call for more comprehensive experimentation and clinician collaboration/assessment of policy trustworthiness before real-world deployment.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors identify irregular, sparse EHR observations and informative missingness as challenges; they state existing RL approaches often discretize/impute data and model-free methods lack patient-dynamics simulation for exploring alternative paths.
legacy_cells.FR: The paper demonstrates retrospective offline policy evaluation and latent trajectory reconstruction, not identified counterfactual treatment effects, prospective patient survival benefit, or real-world deployment. Estimated mortality and OPE metrics are proxies; authors report no counterfactual ground truth.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M6 Rollout service; M7 Outcome & causal layer; M8 Planner; M9 Safety & governance
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Keep the learned patient/scene simulator separate from the planner objective; constrain candidate actions and report closed-loop decision quality alongside model fidelity.
legacy_cells.FX: Title and abstract, PDF pp. 1–2; methodology and model architecture, pp. 3–8; experiments/results and Tables 1–2, pp. 8–13; ethics statement and action/data appendices, pp. 18–20; broader impact and limitations, pp. 21–22. Also reviewed relevant extracted appendices/tables, including robustness and external-task results. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
